channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Redemptor Hominis: more important than ever
item.description: Today, in a global culture dominated by the notion that everything in the human condition is plastic, malleable, and changeable by acts of human will — the insistence that nothing is given — the question on which the future of Christian mission and service to the world depends is, “Who are we?” Are we simply congealed stardust, the happy but accidental byproduct of billions of years of random cosmic biochemical forces?

item.title: Archbishop Lori announces clergy appointments, including associate pastors
item.description: See new clergy appointments including pastors, associate pastors, deacons, and more.

item.title: Church is holy by Christ’s presence, not human perfection, pope says
item.description: The Catholic Church is both a community made up of fragile and limited human beings and a divine reality, Pope Leo XIV said at his weekly general audience.

item.title: Amid U.S. and Israel-Iran war, Palestinian sisters find refuge in prayer at Jerusalem hospital
item.description: Among the belongings Asma Isyed, 68, brought from her West Bank village of Zababdeh in October were a small Bible and a booklet of prayers by St. Mariam Baouardy, a Palestinian saint.

item.title: Prayer, unity essential as conflict spreads to Gulf States, says apostolic vicar of region
item.description: The apostolic vicar of Southern Arabia warned that the current military escalation in the Persian Gulf amid the U.S. and Israel-Iran war is a conflict with "ancient roots" that poses a serious threat to the Middle East and the wider world.

item.title: 9 ‘perpetual pilgrims’ to travel patriotic East Coast route in 2026 National Eucharistic Pilgrimage
item.description: Nine young adults have been selected as "perpetual pilgrims" to travel with the Eucharist along the East Coast this summer in the third National Eucharistic Pilgrimage. The pilgrims -- five men and four women -- will participate in the pilgrimage's full route, which begins May 24 in Florida and reaches Maine before ending in Philadelphia July 5 for U.S. semiquincentennial celebrations.

item.title: What we’re becoming: AI and future of human dignity
item.description: If we approach "the AI Revolution" with only an eye to potential benefits, we'll blindly accept the deleterious consequences to human life and society. We'll automate ourselves into irrelevance without meaning to. We'll outsource our humanity one convenience at a time.

item.title: Expert: Violent 764 group a ‘growing problem’ targeting vulnerable kids online
item.description: A number of violent extremist groups, led by minors and young adults, are increasingly targeting kids online -- in some cases, with deadly results.

item.title: Cardinal Parolin questions whether missiles, bombs are solution to Iranian people’s aspirations
item.description: The Vatican secretary of state appealed for peace and diplomacy on the fifth day of the U.S. and Israel-Iran war, warning that recognition of any country's right to wage "preventive war" according to their own criteria would risk the world "being set ablaze."

item.title: St. Frances connects from long range to deny Mount Carmel for BCL Tournament crown
item.description: With some sizzling long-range shooting (14-for-30) in the 55th edition of the BCL Tournament final, top-seeded St. Frances rallied from an early five-point deficit to grab a seven-point halftime advantage on the way to a 67-55 victory.
